original_title: Batman, Lord of the Rings, and Harry Potter Feature in First Trailer for Skydance, the Newly Named Parent Company for a Merged Warner Bros. and Paramount

en.title: Skydance Unveils Empire: Batman, LOTR, and Harry Potter Under One New Banner
en.summary: A seismic shift in Hollywood is underway as Skydance emerges as the new parent company for Warner Bros. and Paramount. The newly revealed trailer hints at a vast IP portfolio, sparking excitement and questions among fans worldwide.
en.body:
The entertainment landscape has been dramatically reshaped with the confirmation of **Skydance** as the new parent company overseeing a merged **Warner Bros.** and **Paramount**. This colossal deal, reportedly valued at $110 billion, brings iconic studios and their vast libraries of intellectual property under one unified banner, led by **David Ellison** and backed by his father, **Larry Ellison**. While the corporate maneuvers have faced regulatory scrutiny and concerns about job losses, the opposition has seemingly subsided, paving the way for this new era.

A bombastic trailer has officially dropped, offering a tantalizing glimpse into the sheer scale of **Skydance's** new domain. The trailer prominently showcased beloved franchises such as **DC Comics** (including **Batman**), **The Lord of the Rings**, and **Harry Potter**, suggesting a future where these worlds might converge or be explored in new, interconnected ways. The voiceover declared, "These brands are more than a destination, they are the launch pad." This move positions **Skydance** not just as a conglomerate, but as a "creative-first home" aiming to empower these storied studios with a "more powerful engine" for content creation.

## A New Era for Iconic Franchises

The implications for fans of **Batman**, **The Lord of the Rings**, and **Harry Potter** are profound, especially within the gaming community. While the trailer itself doesn't explicitly announce a new game, its inclusion of these powerhouse franchises alongside **Paramount's** own IP, such as **Star Trek** and **Mission: Impossible**, hints at ambitious future projects. We know that a new **Lord of the Rings** game is reportedly in development from **Crystal Dynamics**, the studio behind the recent **Tomb Raider** reboot trilogy. Furthermore, recent behind-the-scenes developments suggest that the **Harry Potter** franchise is also entering a "new era" for gaming, potentially signaling major updates or new titles beyond the already successful **Hogwarts Legacy**.

## What the Merger Means for Gamers

This consolidation could lead to unprecedented cross-franchise collaborations in gaming. Imagine **Batman** teaming up with Gandalf, or a **Harry Potter** spell being used in Middle-earth. While such ideas remain speculative, the sheer breadth of IP now under **Skydance's** control makes them a possibility. The inclusion of **Batman** in the trailer, despite no specific game being announced, fuels speculation about the future of the **DC video game** slate, which has seen recent successes with titles like **Suicide Squad: Kill the Justice League** and the **Gotham Knights** title. The industry will be watching closely to see how **Skydance** leverages these beloved universes, balancing the legacy of **Warner Bros.** and **Paramount** with innovative new directions.

## What's Next

Details on specific gaming projects stemming from the **Skydance** merger have not yet been announced. Fans should keep an eye on official announcements from **Skydance**, **Warner Bros. Games**, and **Crystal Dynamics** for further updates on the **Lord of the Rings** and **Harry Potter** gaming initiatives, as well as potential new ventures for **DC Comics** properties.

content_raw: Once merged, Harry Potter, Lord of the Rings, and Game of Thrones company Warner Bros. will exist alongside Paramount as a sub-brand of Skydance. The historic film and TV studios are being slapped together by David Ellison and backed by his billionaire dad Larry Ellison in a deal worth $110 billion, following a hostile bid for WB last year and despite various regulatory blocks that have attempted to scupper the deal in the U.S. and abroad. Concern has been raised that the merger may lead to thousands of job losses through corporate consolidation, afford control over a huge chunk of Hollywood to the Ellison family, and in turn risk the independence of news networks such as CNN. However, opposition to the deal has now largely melted away and, with the merger's completion appearing imminent, Ellison has now confirmed that "Skydance" will be the name of his soon-to-be enormous entertainment empire. The Warner Bros. and Paramount branding will still be kept for their relevant subdivisions. Indeed, a bombastic new trailer for Skydance has also been revealed, showcasing the vast swath of Warner Bros. and Paramount intellectual property that Skydance will have access to, including the DC Comics, Lord of the Rings, and Harry Potter franchises. What once was the peak, is now just the beginning. Paramount and Warner Bros. shaped over a century of culture. By combining them, we aren't rewriting history — we're equipping these iconic studios with a more powerful engine. Together, we are Skydance: a creative-first home for… pic.twitter.com/uInLRY3IrE — David Ellison (@ellisonskydance) October 2, 2026 "These brands are more than a destination, they are the launch pad," a voiceover for the trailer states, in a script that sounds like it was written by an AI. "They don't just live on screens, they move through culture. Each one, distinct. Built on story. Driven by technology. A new center of gravity. A constellation. A shared vision to go beyond. Look up. What once was the peak, is now just the beginning." Whatever that's supposed to mean, the trailer includes clips from notable WB and Paramount movies and TV series such as Inception, Titanic, Superman, Barbie, Minecraft, The Godfather, The Sopranos, Star Trek, The Matrix, Game of Thrones, The Shawshank Redemption, Casablanca, A Star is Born, Grease, Sinners, Forrest Gump, Dune, Ferris Bueller's Day Off, The Great Gatsby, and Euphoria. A selection of brand logos shown at the end of the trailer highlights that Skydance will own Paramount, WB, DC Comics, CNN, Paramount+, CBS, Nickelodeon, and HBO Max, plus MTV, TCM, Showtime, Adult Swim, Comedy Central, Cartoon Network, Eurosport, Miramax, NewLine Cinema, Animal Planet, the UK's Channel 5, and many, many more. The deal that will cement ownership of all this under Skydance is now expected to close on October 6, the companies have said.
